row_semantics: Trigger conditions and corresponding execution actions for ambient lamp breathing control.
column_semantics: Trigger Conditions: Specifies the conditions under which the ambient lamp breathing control logic is activated.
Execution Actions: Describes the actions taken by the system when the trigger conditions are met, including breathing mode switching and brightness modulation.

core_entities.name: DoorFR1LampBrthngCmd_1
core_entities.description: Local control module command signal for ambient lamp breathing speed.

core_entities.name: DoorFR1LampBrtnsCmd_1
core_entities.description: Driver control module for ambient lamp breathing.

core_entities.name: ZCU
core_entities.description: Zone Control Unit, sends breathing mode commands to the ambient lamp.

core_conditions.condition: Ambient lamp is in bright state
core_conditions.details: Received local control module command signal DoorFR1LampBrthngCmd_1 is not equal to 0x0 (No Request) and ambient light synchronization signal AmbtLghtLHRollingCtr_1 is present.

core_outputs.details: The ambient lamp performs brightness modulation from 0%-100%-0% according to the breathing command period DoorFR1LampBrthngCmd_1.
When different breathing modes are switched, the current breathing stops immediately, and the next breathing mode is switched.

core_timing_constraints.details: For 0%-100% step change modulation (DoorFR1LampBrthngCmd_1 = 0x1), the cycle is 500ms (250ms at 100% brightness, 250ms at 0% brightness). For 0%-100% gradual change modulation (DoorFR1LampBrthngCmd_1 = 0x2), the cycle is 1000ms (500ms at 100% brightness, 500ms at 0% brightness).

For 0%-100% gradual change modulation (DoorFR1LampBrthngCmd_1 = 0x3-0xC, 0xE), the time A is calculated as RateX * (0.5 - AmbtLampBrthngRateXholdoffPercent), where RateX is the received breathing mode period.

engineering_interpretation: This table defines the logic for controlling the ambient lamp's breathing function based on local control commands and ZCU-sent breathing modes, specifying how brightness changes and mode switches occur under different conditions.
